top_story: A fragile US-Iran ceasefire came under acute pressure on 7 May as violence in and around the Strait of Hormuz escalated from a reported US attack on an Iranian oil tanker and subsequent missile fire at US naval units to acknowledged US retaliatory strikes on targets inside Iran. By late evening, both sides were signaling containment rather than open rupture, but the exchange showed how quickly maritime incidents can reopen a broader military front centered on one of the world’s most sensitive energy corridors. Inside Iran, this external confrontation is unfolding alongside a harsher domestic climate marked by near-daily secret executions, pressure on families, and an internet blackout that limits scrutiny and narrows public space. The combined picture is of an Iranian state managing external escalation and internal repression in parallel, raising the risk that regional crisis and domestic coercion will reinforce each other.
